samples.summary: Compiled JS copies of the two changed ops scripts still exist in the tree and create Yorkie clients with no `authTokenInjector`
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.js:160` and `:164` build `new sdk_1.default.Client({...})` with no `authTokenInjector` (grep for `authTokenInjector` in that file returns nothing), and `packages/backend/scripts/migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.js` (+ matching `.d.ts`/`.js.map`) is the same stale build of the other changed script. Since this PR makes enforcement the default, an operator (or tooling) invoking the emitted `.js` rather than the `.ts` attaches anonymously and is denied on any deployment that registered the webhook methods — the exact failure the new injectors exist to prevent. Either delete/ignore these artifacts or regenerate them as part of this change.

samples.summary: Top-level design doc still states the auth webhook is off by default, contradicting the flipped `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` default
samples.evidence: `docs/design/sharing.md:208-219` — "This is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment, which puts the controller in shadow mode" — and `:233` "with the flag at its default the client-side checks are what stands there". `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts` now makes unset mean enforce, so this consumer of the flag's contract describes the old behaviour (and other files in the branch, e.g. self-hosting.md, were updated).

samples.summary: docs package's read-only wrapper and editor comments still claim the webhook ships in shadow mode by default
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:39-42` ("the Yorkie auth webhook — ships in shadow mode by default … so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary") and `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4411-4415` ("ships in shadow mode unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`, so in a stock deployment this is the write boundary"). The notes-package twin was rewritten in this diff (`packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:60-66`) but its docs-package original — the module it explicitly mirrors — was left describing the old default.

samples.summary: New comment added by this change contradicts the change's own default flip
samples.evidence: The comment block added at `packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:439-447` says "the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default and so may not refuse the write either", while `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts` in the same PR makes enforcement the default and `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:60-66` says the opposite. Two comments in the same package now state opposite contracts for the same flag.

samples.summary: Two more design docs still reason from the shadow-mode default
samples.evidence: `docs/design/template-gallery.md:668` ("with `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset the auth webhook only …") and `docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:301` ("(`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false`), so the one CRDT write on this path …") both describe the pre-change default. The nested-doc one is additionally outside the CI ref-check's reach (only top-level design docs are scanned).

samples.summary: `LakehouseView` accepts a `readOnly` prop but publishes presence with an ungated `doc.update()` — the one presence write left outside the new rule
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/lakehouse-view.tsx:48` takes `readOnly = false`, and `:89-98` runs `doc.update((_, presence) => presence.set({ activeTabId, … }))` unconditionally on mount — the same mount-time presence seed this PR gated in `YorkieStore`'s constructor (`yorkie-store.ts:110`), `board-view.tsx:602`, `slides-view.tsx:1147` and `pdf-collab.tsx:134`. Today the shared route renders `SharedLakehouseUnavailable` (`shared-document.tsx:281`) and `document-detail.tsx:721` passes no `readOnly`, so it is not reachable on a viewer mount — but the prop exists, and the moment it is passed true this write wedges that viewer's sync under enforce-by-default.

samples.summary: The share-token uploader handed to `NotesView` has the docs contract (throws) not the notes contract (resolve `null` after telling the user)
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.ts:40` returns a `DocsImageUpload` that lets `postShareTokenImage` errors propagate, while `packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:19-26` defines `UploadImage` as "resolve `null` when the host has already reported the failure … a rejected promise is treated the same way, with a console entry". The authenticated route wraps its uploader precisely for this (`notes-detail.tsx:203-221` toasts and returns `null`). So on the new shared note route an upload failure (413, network, 401) is dropped to the console with no user-visible message.

samples.summary: `readOnlyNoteStore`'s reader allowlist silently no-ops any store member that is not part of `NoteStore`, including future lifecycle methods
samples.evidence: `NOTE_STORE_READERS` (packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:21-29) lists only the seven interface readers; every other function member falls to `noop`. `MemNoteStore.setLocalAuthor` (used at `packages/notes/src/view/blame-gutter.test.ts:125`) is already such a member, and a lifecycle method (e.g. a future `YorkieNoteStore.dispose()`, which would unsubscribe the CRDT listeners) would be silently swallowed on viewer mounts rather than failing loudly. Verified no production caller does this today (`YorkieNoteStore` only implements the interface — yorkie-note-store.ts:150-458), so this is a latent trap rather than a live break.

samples.summary: Adding `mode` to the store-mount effect's deps makes a mode change tear down and rebuild the Yorkie store
samples.evidence: `mobile-slides-view.tsx:145-164` now re-runs on `mode`, disposing the store and firing `onStoreReady(null)` then a new store. Both current callers pass a constant (`slides-detail.tsx:838` `mode="edit"`, `shared-document.tsx:627` `mode={readOnly ? "view" : "edit"}` derived from the resolved role), so nothing breaks today; a caller that ever toggles mode in place would drop the lifted store/editor state (selection, undo stack) as a side effect of what looks like a render-only prop.

samples.summary: Comment in the PDF comment store no longer holds now that read-only mounts seed nothing
samples.evidence: `pdf-comment-store.ts:123` says "Seeded at bootstrap (initialPdfRoot); guard only for legacy docs", but `pdf-collab.tsx:211` now passes `initialRoot={readOnly ? {} : initialPdfRoot()}`, so an un-seeded `root.comments` is also the normal viewer-first case. The `if (!root.comments)` guard makes this harmless; only the comment is wrong.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.js:160 and :164 construct `new sdk_1.default.Client({...})` with no `authTokenInjector`, and packages/backend/scripts/migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.js:125 does the same (`new sdk_1.default.Client({ rpcAddr, apiKey })`). A repo-wide grep for `authTokenInjector` matches neither file. The corresponding .ts sources now attach service tokens (copy-yorkie-documents.ts:255-263, migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts:344-348) with comments stating enforcement is now the default and anonymous attaches are refused. The .js/.d.ts/.js.map artifacts are neither ignored (root .gitignore only ignores `dist`; packages/backend/.gitignore ignores only /dist, /build, /node_modules) nor regenerated (packages/backend/tsconfig.json:30 excludes `scripts` from compilation), so they are frozen committed duplicates that will never gain the injector — and they are already stale in other ways (the .js still uses a local replaceRoot/JSON snapshot path at lines 140-150 while the .ts uses `snapshotJsonRoot`). No guard makes them unreachable: running `node scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.js` needs no other entry point. This is a duplicated/stale copy of a changed contract, inside the blast-radius lane, and I found no ground to refute it.
